author: Taylor Kalin
source: Chowdhry and Loureiro, JPP91E148 and arXiv2508.13081v1
scope: Internal mathematical comment, not a full MHD rerun or exhaustive proof that every source statement has been adjudicated.

supported_findings.result: Nonlinear pressure formula fails the stated EOS; correct solution is Bernoulli/exponential. Finite-C2 bremsstrahlung form has zero initial transformed cooling rate.
Correct scalar pressure is generally not a time-only rescaling of the initial parabola for nontrivial bremsstrahlung cooling; global affine force closure does not follow.
Common scalar positive-pressure flow preserves initial ordering. Printed outflow deceleration for 0<xi<eta,P0X>0 requires negative central total pressure.
supported_findings.class: exact conditional sign and order statement

supported_findings.result: At fixed finite coefficients, finite positive eta_c, and alpha2/3 or1, Ic is positive finite; cooling/magnetic ratio tends to zero. Tail-only substitution loses leading constant.
supported_findings.class: conditional endpoint limit, not finite-window rejection

supported_findings.result: Leading inverse-square scalar force requires A^3=9eta_c/2, not9eta_c/4; generic finite thermal coefficient gives first8/9 correction, with special4/3 control separated.
Time ratio requires division by Gamma_y0; separate gamma-1 clock convention retained. Printed1-b to b-1 reversal masked by bremsstrahlung square.
Displayed steady algebra passes; layer-fit, enhancement, thinness and sub-Alfvenic bounds require additional parameter inequalities. Existence alone does not prove stability.
supported_findings.class: preserved positive algebra with domain/stability qualification

positive_controls: Final cooling-law and Newtonian/relativistic caveats credited
